## 0.4.2

- The microphone meter reads like a real meter. Your normal voice fills most of the bar and shouting maxes it out, and the bar turns from green to yellow to red as you get louder.
- A smaller Listening pill that covers less of your screen.
- History is cleaner: each dictation shows just its time and length.
- Top apps on the Overview page works again and shows the apps you dictate into most.

Also in this release (first shipped in the 0.4.1 beta):
- A setup guide for new users. The first time Dicta starts, a short full-screen guide checks your microphone, lets you pick your dictation key, and has you try it: hold the key to talk, or double-tap for hands-free. It shows the two shortcuts worth knowing, lets you choose how your words come out by example, and helps you add your own free Groq key if you want Rewrite. You can run it again any time from the tray, and nothing changes until you press Finish.
- Settings looks and works like it always did. The dark Settings window with Overview, History, Dictionary, Snippets, Shortcuts and Learning is back, with a few new options added in the same style: a writing style for each app, and the option to use names visible on screen.
- Clearer, smaller notices. When something needs your attention, Dicta now shows a short title and one line, sized to fit. If a paste can't land, one small card says your words are on the clipboard, with Insert here and Dismiss.
- A proper installer. Setup now matches Dicta's dark look, updates install in place without asking you to uninstall first, and you can open Dicta right away when setup finishes.
- Clicking Dicta in the taskbar opens it. Clicking a pinned Dicta icon while it's running now opens Settings instead of doing nothing.

And from the 0.4.0 beta:
- Long dictations are fast and light. Dicta now transcribes while you are still talking, cutting at natural pauses, so on an NVIDIA PC even a three-minute dictation is ready about a second after you stop. Memory stays about the same however long you talk: a three-minute dictation on the CPU used to take nearly 5 GB and now stays under 1 GB. If one part fails, Dicta transcribes the whole recording again instead of giving up.
- Pasting into Google Docs works again. Dictating into a Doc could type your words letter by letter, or not land at all, especially right after you had copied something from Chrome. Dicta now keeps Chrome's clipboard data intact, returns to the window you were dictating into before it pastes, and checks one last time that you are still there. Your clipboard is restored afterwards, and anything you copied privately, such as from a password manager, is never kept.
- Your words are never lost when a paste can't land. If Dicta can't deliver a dictation because you switched away, a small card keeps the text so you can insert it where you are now or copy it. It only appears when delivery actually failed.
- Each app gets the right style. In AI chat apps, terminals and code editors, Dicta keeps commands exactly as you said them ("ls -la" stays lowercase). You can choose a style for any app in Settings, and your Raw, Light or Full choice always applies.
- Full cleanup is faster and writes plainer punctuation. Dicta keeps its connection to the rewrite service open between dictations, so each Full rewrite starts sooner, and it uses commas and ordinary punctuation instead of long dashes. Number ranges such as "9 – 5" stay as they are.
- Dicta updates itself. It checks for a new version shortly after starting and once a day, and the tray menu offers "Update to …" when one is ready.
- Uses less memory and disk. The graphics-card helper gives back about 1 GB of memory after 30 seconds idle, and starting the GPU no longer re-reads or re-copies its 500 MB runtime file on every launch, so it gets ready much faster.
- Spanish is retired for now. The language choice is gone from Settings. If you had Spanish selected, it keeps working, and you can switch to English at any time.
- Smaller fixes: thousands separators and "ten" stay intact in rewrites, spoken list items are tidied, learning retries a failed save instead of dropping it, and leftover temporary files are cleaned up.
